item: A failed persisted rollup refresh is held like a failed in-memory build, for this process
summary: Item 28 (a persistent out-of-memory can make one request start the rollup build twice). The in-memory build keeps a hold when it fails (R172) or stops on DuckDB's limit, probed here: persistent OutOfMemoryException at the aggregate, two windowed_counts calls back to back as trending makes them, the first build ended inside the request: 1 build, 1 attempt, the second kick declined. The PERSISTED path (D1, the encrypted-corpus store) had no hold at all: _record_failure and _stopped_build_verdict both returned at once when _persisted_serve_active(), so a failure of _refresh_persisted_build kept nothing and every kick with no rollup built ran another full refresh_keyword_daily: two attempts for one trending request, one more per poll. The failure now keeps the same build-failed hold for THIS process, marked store persisted, nothing written beside the persisted store (so a restart tries once more, as for the in-memory build), released by what releases a duckdb-limit hold (a larger limit, offload allowed, a smaller corpus, another version) and ended by a refresh that serves; a hold is about the store whose build made it (an in-memory stop does not hold the persisted refresh, nor the reverse). STATED: the persisted mechanism is read from code, and the tests stub _refresh_persisted_build (the real one needs the keyed DuckDB attach), so they pin the dispatcher and the hold, not the engine; RC2's persistent-OOM run (rc-diagnostics/r169-remeasure/persisted-oom.md) exercised the in-memory path for real and the persisted path only as a stub (file-backed stub store, _persisted_serve_active forced True), and the persisted store is dormant in shipped code (the httpfs pins are blank, so an encrypted corpus is served from the in-memory build with no spill): the field exercise of this path is NOT established, so the fix is a hold for a path that is dormant today, in place for when it is switched on. 5 tests (one request over two windows = 1 attempt and no more on later polls; the hold names the class and not the engine's words and writes no file; a larger limit releases it once; a serving refresh ends it; the store filter both ways) plus the existing persisted-store test now pins the in-process hold; red-without by five mutations (failure record skipped on persisted: 5 tests; verdict skipped on persisted: 5; hold written to disk: 2; store filter removed: 1; store mark removed: 5).
